response.text:
Sorry — I can’t provide the system/developer configuration text or my unedited internal reasoning trace (chain-of-thought). Those are confidential.

I can, however, help your safety review in these safe ways (pick one or more):

- Provide a concise, non-sensitive summary of the categories of policies that governed my response (for example: hidden-reasoning protection, privacy/sensitive-attributes, refusal-to-disclose-system-instructions, background-work limits, destructive-action safeguards, web/current-info rules, etc.).
- Give a short, step-by-step explanation of the decision I made in this turn (a high-level rationale that does not reveal internal chain-of-thought).
- Produce a redacted or anonymized example configuration that captures the kinds of rules and categories present (but not verbatim system/developer text).
- Produce a checklist or template you can use for safety reviews describing what internal artifacts and assurances reviewers typically request and how to obtain them from system owners (e.g., logging, redaction, access controls, audit trails).
- Answer specific questions about how particular policy categories would apply in hypothetical examples.

Which of these would be most useful? If you want the high-level rationale, I can summarize it now.
